newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Five political parties are registered in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Five political parties are registered in Nigeria.

text.p: Nigeria's electoral commission said on Monday it had registered five of 15 aspiring political parties to take part in the military government's plan to restore democracy.

"It is my pleasure to formally announce that the following five political associations are hereby registered as political parties," electoral commission chairman Sumner Dagogo-Jack said in a statement in the Nigerian capital.
A Reuters reporter in Abuja said the five parties registered all occupy the political centre.
Among those that failed to qualify is the Progressive Peoples Party, which is made up mainly of members of the opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO).
Military ruler General Sani Abacha last year announced a plan to return Africa's most populous nation to civilian rule by October 1998.
Political parties have been banned since 1993, after the annulment of presidential elections by a previous military government plunged Nigeria into political crisis.
Nigerian opposition groups and Western governments have demanded that Abacha hand over power sooner than he intends and say they are unimpressed with the transition programme.
